items.title: Midwestern Winter Awareness Weeks Begin
items.body: The National Weather Service lists winter-preparedness awareness periods beginning November 8 in Indiana and Michigan and November 9 in Illinois; Wisconsin follows November 16. This is scheduled education, not evidence of an imminent storm. Check heating, flashlights, medication supplies and travel plans while conditions are calm.
items.source: National Weather Service preparedness calendar · Nov 2026

items.title: National Weather Service Sees Later-Week Pattern Changes
items.body: The Weather Prediction Center's November 8 extended discussion notes possible Pacific Northwest unsettled weather and a later cold rain or inland snow setup in the Northeast. Forecast uncertainty remains; consult local NWS warnings before taking action.

items.title: Winter Vehicle Kit: Useful Before the First Breakdown
items.body: NWS winter guidance emphasizes risks from slick travel, cold exposure and utility outages. A small vehicle kit can prioritize warm layers, water, a flashlight, charged phone power, medication and a means to alert help. Avoid running a car in an enclosed space. Preparedness is a routine, not a prediction.
items.source: National Weather Service winter preparedness guidance

items.title: Why Was the E-4B 'Doomsday Plane' Flying?
items.body: Reports describe an E-4B Nightwatch departing Offutt Air Force Base on November 5 and flying east toward the Washington area. The mission and passengers have not been publicly confirmed. The E-4B supports continuity of government and military command during emergencies, but also flies training and senior-official support missions. A visible flight alone is not evidence of an impending attack. Watch for independently corroborated changes in posture, not dramatic aircraft nicknames.
items.source: U.S. Air Force E-4B fact sheet; November 7 flight report
